newsitem.title: CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC: Central African Republic names new prime minister.
newsitem.headline: Central African Republic names new prime minister.

text.p: Central African Republic's president named outgoing foreign minister Michel Gbezzera-Bria on Thursday to head a national unity government to end a cycle of military, political and ethnic violence in the country.

President Ange-Felix Patasse nominated Gbezzera-Bria, 51, a career administrator, in a decree that follows a January 25 peace deal brokered by African mediators to end the impoverished nation's third army mutiny in under a year.
A former ambassador to the United Nation and foreign minister in the outgoing government, Gbezzera-Bria would form and head a "Government of Action for the Defence of Democracy", the decree said.
He replaces Jean-Paul Ngoumpande, who was nominated in June 1996.

In an earlier gesture of national reconciliation, the paramilitary gendarmerie on Tuesday freed 35 people detained by French soldiers during violent incidents on January 4 and 5. They included seven mutineers.
Mutinies in April and May began over pay and conditions but turned into a campaign to oust Patasse, a northern civilian who won presidential elections in 1993.
The latest mutiny, which began on November 15, degenerated into ethnic feuding. The mutineers were from the minority Yakoma tribe of former military leader Andre Kolingba.
Estimates of those killed in the mutinies range from scores to several hundred. French troops, in the country under a defence pact, stepped in to restore order.

The presidents of Gabon, Chad, Mali and Burkina Faso launched the mediation process in December at the behest of a Franco-African summit. Mali's widely respected former military leader, Amadou Toumani Toure, brokered the deal.

The peace blueprint also envisaged amnesties, restoration of constitutional legality under the democratic transition and a 500-strong African peacekeeping force with soldiers from Burkina Faso, Chad, Gabon, Mali, Senegal and Togo.
